notes: Lebanon has held no general census since 1932. Population by caza (Beirut Governorate plus the Mount Lebanon cazas of Baabda, Metn, Chouf, Aley, Keserwan) uses the best available estimate, a 2017-2019 Central Administration of Statistics / UNDP household survey — the most recent sub-city figure that exists, but one that predates the 2019 economic crisis, subsequent refugee-population shifts, and 2024 conflict-driven displacement entirely; this staleness is disclosed rather than presented as current. No real employment data exists: jobs are a flat 40% of resident population, redistributed across OSM buildings weighted by floor area only. Commute flows are an unconstrained gravity model with no real O/D anchor. The airport's demand figure does use real, sourced traffic (2023 total, the last pre-crisis-disruption year) with no correspondence adjustment needed — 2023 transit-passenger share was under 0.1%, confirming this isn't a connecting hub — but this is one special point, not a characterization of the map's overall methodology.
